the Chinese and Vietnamese governments, as well as the environmental protection agencies, are increasingly aware of the importance of information and the use of information in environmental protection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of new forms of informational environmental governance in China and Vietnam.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Chinese and Vietnamese cases are characterized by a limited emergence of informational governance, but that this is a process that is still unfolding.
the Chinese and Vietnamese environmental governance systems are in the process of being transformed from a traditional regulatory-based model to an information- based model.
the informationalization of environmental governance in China and Vietnam is still very much in its infancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the environmental problems of China and Vietnam can be seen as the product of a complex mix of factors, including the rapid economic and social changes, the lack of environmental awareness and knowledge, and the weak environmental governance.
we have found that the use of the Internet in China and Vietnam is not a simple matter of access and use.
the environmental information system in China has been developed to a certain extent, but there is much room for improvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the role of information is not just about the production of new information or the dissemination of information to the general public, but about the way in which the production and dissemination of information is embedded in and shapes social relations.
information is not just a resource for governance, but also a governance resource, with its own dynamics, and with its own implications.
information and information technologies can help us to better understand and govern the environmental impacts of global supply chains.
